source_pdf: 312 Affidavits by Indians who accepted land patents under protest 1928 [1 of 3].pdf

extraction.Name: Hermos Merrivall
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want it, but that he receipted for it and took it because he was told in the Agency Office that he would have to pay taxes on the land or lose it if he didnt take it
extraction.Recorded patent: had it recorded at Hot Springs, So. Dak.
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: he has not deeded or mortgaged any part of his land, and that it was sold for taxes and he redeemed it and that later it was sold again and he did not redeem it
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: it was sold for taxes and he redeemed it and that later it was sold again and he did not redeem it
extraction.Occupation/Income: farming on his fathers allotment for a living
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent and in fair health; broke all the time and has a hard time getting along; has not received any aid from the Government, County or State since his patent was issued; mother, wife and two children are dependent on him for support; document subscribed and sworn November 2, 1928
